contributions: Comprehensive textbook covering algorithms for decision making under uncertainty
Cross-disciplinary synthesis drawing from economics, psychology, neuroscience, computer science, engineering, and mathematics
Applications including aircraft collision avoidance, automated driving, breast cancer screening, financial portfolio allocation, and distributed wildfire surveillance
limitations: Algorithm implementations prioritize interpretability over efficiency, so industrial applications may need alternative implementations
Requires mathematical maturity and prior exposure to multivariable calculus, linear algebra, and probability
Intended audience is limited to advanced undergraduates, graduate students, and professionals
methods: The book covers multiple computational approaches to decision making: explicit programming, supervised learning (behavioral cloning), optimization-based search, planning with dynamic models, and reinforcement learning. All algorithms are implemented in the Julia programming language with interpretability prioritized over efficiency. The text uses figures, examples, and exercises to convey intuition behind various approaches.
results: N/A - this is a textbook preface and introduction, not a research paper with empirical results. The book covers applications across aircraft collision avoidance, automated driving, breast cancer screening (comparing systems via quality-adjusted life years, false positive rates, and mammogram counts), financial consumption/portfolio allocation, and distributed wildfire surveillance using drone teams.
tldr: This textbook provides a broad introduction to algorithms for decision making under uncertainty, covering mathematical formulations, planning, and reinforcement learning with implementations in Julia.
